head: claude/ict-scalp-exit-head-20260906
title: MI-150: ship the M20 exit-head consumer into ict_scalp (annotate-only, disarmed)
body:
## What this lands, and what it deliberately does not

**Lands:** the M20 exit-head **consumer** in `ict_scalp` — the wiring MI-146 § "Recommendation 2" identified as the only passed-gate work in the whole 468-cell matrix blocked on missing code. Operator-approved 2026-09-06 ("Yes on MI 146").

**Does not land:** any arming. `ICT_SCALP_EXIT_HEAD_MODE` defaults to `annotate` and **no leg declares `exit_head_action`**, so the path is byte-for-byte inert. Arming is Tier-3 and is *proposed*, not taken.

> ### ⚠️ The brief for this work omitted a standing operator decision. Read this before arming anything.
>
> All five candidate cells carry a **2026-08-23 `SHIP BLOCKED` operator verdict** in `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json` that **cancelled the queued Tier-3 ship**. It names its own precondition: *"Re-grade to shipped/passed_unshipped only AFTER a consumer exists in the ict_scalp unit."* **This PR satisfies that precondition and nothing else.**
>
> And for `ict_scalp_sol_5m` the same ref records that **its pass does not survive re-partitioning** — the 4-arm screen flips it to `honest_negative` when folds are cut 12 trades later, its live-parity `beats_hard` is **16/23** (clearing by 2 points of 46, so one fold the other way fails it), and its AUC spread across arms (0.0034) was the *smallest* of the three legs, so the AUC gave no warning (`BL-20260815-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-MATRIX-DISAGREES-WITH-THE-4-ARM-SCREEN`). A session arming off MI-146's headline AUC table would be arming over a cancelled ship.

## ⛔ It cannot score a single leg today — measured, not assumed

`/api/diag/shadow_stats`, read 2026-09-06 (`last_seen 10:00:01Z`): the live mirror publishes **exactly two** exit-head artifacts — `exit-head-donchian-1h-v1` (advisory) and `exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1` (shadow), count 52 each — and **both are `tf: 1h`**, while all 8 `ict_scalp` legs are 5m or 15m. `maybe_score_exit_head`'s in-distribution guard therefore fail-closes on every one, and the consumer records `decision_state: not_scored`.

**The blocker moved from missing CODE to missing ARTIFACT; it did not clear.** I am reporting that rather than implying a soak is accruing. Registered as `OI-20260906-ICT-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-CONSUMER-SHIPPED-AND-CANNOT-SCORE-UNTIL-A-SCALP-HEAD-IS-PUBLISHED`.

## Mirrored, not re-implemented

The firing rule was **factored out**, not copied — `trend_donchian._exit_head_verdict` is now a delegation shim to `src/runtime/exit_head_apply.exit_head_verdict`, so donchian's behaviour is unchanged and the move is reviewable *as a move*. This copies the repo's own precedent: `_stale_stop_verdict` / `_giveback_verdict` moved to `exit_levers.py` the same way.

`tests/test_exit_head_apply_parity.py` runs **both call sites over one shared case table** (75 assertions), including the peak-vs-`below_half_r` branch that MB-20260716 already got wrong once — a copy that hardcoded `below_half_r` passes every other case and fails exactly those three.

**The in-distribution guard (#6201) is inherited, not restated.** It lives inside `maybe_score_exit_head`; calling the shared scorer is what carries it, one layer above where a second consumer could forget to ask. A test asserts the unit actually passes `family="ict_scalp"`, since a consumer that does not declare its family silently opts out.

## A real gap found while verifying

The exit-head artifact has declared a **`family`** field since `export_exit_head.py:116` and **nothing has ever read it** — the guard gates on `tf` + `symbols` only, while its own docstring says it exists to stop *"an out-of-family score"*. `tf` + `symbols` cannot separate two strategies trading the **same symbol on the same timeframe**, which is exactly `ict_scalp` vs `donchian` on SOLUSDT. Inert while donchian was the only family with a published head; not inert the moment a scalp head ships.

Fixed **caller-opt-in**: `ict_scalp` passes its family, **donchian deliberately still passes nothing**. Its live advisory artifact closes real positions and *what value its `family` field actually carries has not been read from the mirror* (that dir is not on the diag allowlist). Tightening a live money path against an unverified string is how a working exit gate goes quiet. A mismatch logs at **WARNING** naming both values — a silent refusal would be indistinguishable from a naming difference.

## The two exclusions are encoded distinctly

| leg | status | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ict_scalp_5m` (BTC) | `blocked:data_missing_btcusdt` | `not_measured` | **Never measured** — the round skipped it. A candidate the moment its data resolves. |
| `ict_scalp_eth_15m` | `honest_negative` | `harness_only` | **Measured and failed** — `beats_hard` 4/11 against a bar of 8/11. Not a candidate. |

Collapsing those into one "excluded" list would erase *we did not look* vs *we looked and it failed*.

## Measured ratchet effect: **zero**

`tp_geometry` ratchet: **396 live cells / 229 unstamped / ceiling 229**, identical before and after. No slack opened, no ceiling moved. The ratchet counts live cells lacking a `tp_geometry` stamp; this diff adds and removes no cells, changes no leg's `execution`, and touches no `tp_geometry` field. **Run, not reasoned:** `m20_coverage_rollup.validate()` → 0 problems; `check_matrix_config_agreement` / `check_matrix_corpus_agreement` / `check_matrix_bracket_values` / `check_soak_registered` / `check_open_items` / `check_stated_population` / `check_pr_landing` all OK.

## Tests

**93 new assertions** (75 parity + 9 integration + 9 mode/state). **164 passed** across the affected suites (`test_exit_head_shadow`, `test_ict_scalp_*`, `test_exit_head_feature_parity`). The 45 collection errors in this sandbox are a pre-existing `_cffi_backend` gap — **reproduced on clean `main`**, verified by stash.

## Landing

`.github/pr-landing/ict-scalp-exit-head-20260906.json` → **tier 3 / `hold`**. I first declared tier 2 and the guard corrected me; declaring the higher tier is the only safe direction. **Draft; the manager routes the merge.**
